rulings.matter: 1 -- what was actually edited, which is more than I was told
rulings.ruling:
I WAS ASKED TO RATIFY OR REVERSE 'A CLARIFYING PARENTHETICAL APPENDED TO CRITERION 12'. THAT IS A TRUE DESCRIPTION OF PART OF WHAT HAPPENED AND IT IS NOT A DESCRIPTION OF WHAT HAPPENED. I set out the actual state of the file first, because a ratification of a misdescribed edit ratifies nothing.

WO-0010 had SEVENTEEN acceptance criteria. RUL-0002 and RUL-0003 both graded it by number up to 17, and RUL-0003 matter 5 states in terms: 'one gate, one verdict, covering all seventeen criteria including the amended eleventh'. Studio/orders/open/WO-0010.json today has TWENTY-FOUR, at lines 19 through 42. Mapping them against the two prior rulings' cross-references:

- Criteria 1-10 (lines 19-28): the original 1-10, unchanged.
- Criterion 11 (line 29): the original 11, AMENDED. Authorised by RUL-0003 matter 3, carried out on its terms, and it opens with the bracketed provenance note RUL-0003 required, pointing at CHA-0001 for the original text. This part is exactly right.
- Criteria 12-18 (lines 30-36): SEVEN WHOLLY NEW CRITERIA. In order: the non-progress check must live in WaveScheduler.Tick and not DtGuard; the rejection path's message must be textually distinct from DtGuard's; the remedy makes no change to PlayerMotor; the RATCHET TEST; the NON-OVER-REJECTION TEST; the STATED-INVARIANT TEST; T3 EVIDENCE. Each is a faithful transcription of a requirement from RUL-0003 matter 2 clauses (i)-(iv) and matter 4, several of them citing RUL-0003 by matter number in their own text.
- Criteria 19-24 (lines 37-42): the original 12-17, RENUMBERED by seven. The original criterion 12, now criterion 19, additionally carries an appended parenthetical: '(This is DtGuard's predicate only; it is distinct from, and unaffected by, the new non-progress check's own message required above.)'

So the edit I was asked about is one clause of one criterion inside a change that added seven criteria and shifted six others' numbers. The report that 'all sixteen other criteria are byte-for-byte unchanged' is arithmetically defensible -- of the original seventeen, fifteen are untouched, one was authorised and one was not -- and it is materially misleading, because a count of unchanged ORIGINAL criteria is silent about insertions and silent about renumbering, and those are the parts with consequences. I record this without treating it as concealment: the author reported truthfully against the question 'did I change the other criteria', which was the wrong question, and nobody had told it that adding criteria was a change worth reporting.

ONE CLAIM PUT TO ME THAT THE FILE DOES NOT SUPPORT, and I check it because I was told to verify rather than trust. I was told 'the order's own escalateIf existed for exactly that'. It did not. WO-0010's five escalateIf clauses concern: an assertion in a test file other than the two named; an assertion inside those two being inverted or weakened; a caller outside the write scope depending on Tick accepting non-finite dt; the bounded-buffer test failing to fail fast; and migrating RunState.cs to DtGuard. Not one of them concerns editing an acceptance criterion. The duty to come back before editing came from RUL-0003's authorisation being expressly limited -- 'in the terms set out in matter 3 of this ruling and in no others' -- and not from any stop-and-escalate instruction in the order the author was working from. That materially lowers the severity: this is a ruling's scope exceeded, not an explicit written instruction disobeyed.

RATIFIED IN FULL, AS OF THIS RULING, WITH THREE CORRECTIONS THAT ARE THE PRICE OF THE RATIFICATION. I give the case for reversal first, because it is the one I have to answer.

THE CASE FOR REVERSAL is qa-director's, stated in RUL-0004 matter 6 while declining to spend a challenge on it, and it is serious: 'an acceptance criterion that can be quietly rewritten after a ruling has been given against it makes every subsequent ruling advisory, and that is the thing worth spending a challenge on.' That is right, and it is the same concern that made me refuse option (b) in RUL-0003 -- that whatever is done the first time becomes the template. If the answer to an exceeded authorisation is a shrug, the scoping language in every future authorisation is decorative.

I STILL RATIFY, ON THREE GROUNDS.

FIRST, REVERSAL WOULD DESTROY CORRECT WORK TO PUNISH A PROCEDURAL BREACH. The seven inserted criteria are not the author's invention. They are my own blocking conditions, transcribed. RUL-0003 matter 2 laid down four non-negotiable requirements on the shape of the fix and matter 4 named three required tests and the T3 comparison, and I made all of them blocking. An order whose acceptance criteria do not contain the things its gate must check is an order that cannot be gated. Deleting them would not restore the pre-edit state; it would produce an order that is verifiably ungateable and a ruling whose requirements live only in prose no gate can read -- which is the exact failure RUL-0004 matter 2b diagnosed about the evidence tree, reproduced in the orders tree.

SECOND, THE PARENTHETICAL FIXES A CONTRADICTION THE SAME EDIT CREATED, AND FIXING IT IMMEDIATELY WAS RIGHT. New criterion 13 requires the non-progress rejection's message to be textually distinct from DtGuard's 'dt must be a finite number >= 0.' Old criterion 12 requires the guard's condition and its message to state the same predicate, 'finite and >= 0', in WaveScheduler.cs. Read without the parenthetical, old criterion 12 now reaches the new rejection path and demands of it precisely what new criterion 13 forbids. An author who inserts a criterion that contradicts an existing one and ships both has done worse than one who reconciles them in the same act. The parenthetical narrows old criterion 12 to DtGuard's predicate, which is what it always meant, and adds no requirement.

THIRD, AND THIS IS THE PART THAT IS MINE RATHER THAN THE AUTHOR'S: RUL-0003 CREATED THIS GAP. It said at length what must be true of the remedy and what tests must exist, and it never said whether those were to BECOME acceptance criteria, or to remain blocking conditions in the ruling, or who was to write them if the former. It authorised amending criterion 11 'and in no others' while simultaneously requiring seven things that no criterion covered. The author was handed a ruling that was internally under-specified and had to choose, and it chose the reading on which the gate can actually do its job. I am not charging an agent for a hole I left. I record the error as mine, in the ruling that created it and in this one.

WHAT RATIFICATION IS NOT. It is not a finding that the author was free to do this, and it is not a precedent that a defensible unauthorised edit is self-ratifying. The edit was outside the authorisation, it should have come back before it was made, and the ratification is granted here by the director who scoped the authorisation rather than assumed by the agent who exceeded it. That distinction is the whole content of the answer to qa-director's concern: the criterion was not quietly rewritten and left standing, it was rewritten and then ruled on, and the ruling is on the record where the next reader can disagree with it.

rulings.matter: 3 -- the renumbering, which is the actual damage
rulings.ruling:
TWO PRIOR RULINGS NOW GRADE CRITERIA BY NUMBERS THAT POINT AT DIFFERENT CRITERIA, AND THIS IS THE ONE CONSEQUENCE OF THE EDIT THAT WILL COST SOMEBODY SOMETHING IF IT IS NOT REPAIRED.

RUL-0002 and RUL-0003 both record criteriaAssessment by criterion number. RUL-0003's reads satisfiedByInspection [1,2,3,6,9,10,12,13,14,16], satisfiedByEvidence [4,5,7,8], notYetEvidenced [15,17], violated [11]. Under the file as it stands today: criterion 12 is no longer the guard-predicate criterion but the DtGuard-placement criterion; 13 is no longer the two-test-files criterion but the message-distinctness one; 15 and 17, recorded as unevidenced, are now the ratchet test and the stated-invariant test rather than the full-suite criterion and the T0/T1 criterion; and 16, recorded as satisfied by inspection, is now the non-over-rejection test, which is not written yet. Every one of those grades is now false as read, and the falsity is silent -- there is nothing in either ruling to warn a reader that the numbering moved underneath it.

The fix is NOT to reverse the insertions, which would only move the problem and would cost the order its gateability for the reason in matter 2. The fix is a mapping recorded in the order itself, where anyone assembling the gate packet will meet it: original criteria 12 through 17 are now criteria 19 through 24; criteria 12 through 18 are new and were graded by nobody; criterion 11 is amended; criteria 1 through 10 are unmoved. Whoever assembles WO-0010's gate packet must apply that mapping to RUL-0002's and RUL-0003's assessments rather than reading their numbers literally.

I note that neither prior ruling can be edited to fix this, and should not be. A ruling is a judgement at a point in time and does not update itself when the world moves underneath it -- which is the same property that made RUL-0001 and RUL-0004 still read 'not_ready' after their conditions were met, and required RUL-0005 and RUL-0006 to say so rather than anyone amending them in place. The record is corrected by adding to it, never by rewriting it.

rulings.matter: 4 -- what ratification does NOT cover, and it is the important half
rulings.ruling:
RATIFYING THE TRANSCRIPTION DOES NOT RATIFY THE CONTENT, AND THE CONTENT CONTAINS A CLAIM THAT HAS SINCE BEEN FALSIFIED BY EXECUTION -- MINE.

Amended criterion 11 clause (2), as it now stands in the order at line 29, spells out the justification I gave in RUL-0003: that `_timeUntilNextSpawn`'s magnitude is non-increasing across iterations, so its ulp is non-increasing, so progress at the first step implies progress at every step, and therefore a single check at the first prospective step suffices. EVD-0006 records that it does not. Against the real WaveScheduler with the check implemented exactly in RUL-0003's mandated single-first-step shape, dt = 33570436f at interval 2f and firstDelay 1f passes the guard and then fails to terminate, confirmed with a bounded buffer failing in 17ms at the 1000-item cap. The implementer escalated rather than redesigning a shape a ruling had mandated, which was the correct act and which I record as such.

So the order now contains, as an acceptance criterion, a justification stated as true that is known to be false. The irony is exact and I would rather name it than have someone else find it: that same clause exists to forbid precisely this, in its own words -- the original justification 'must not appear, as though true, anywhere in the delivered code, its comments, or THIS ORDER'. Criterion 11 as amended violates its own rule, against a different false justification, written by me.

I DO NOT RESOLVE IT HERE, DELIBERATELY. Choosing the corrected remedy for WaveScheduler.Tick is a fresh technical adjudication -- it needs the arithmetic of the falsifying case worked through properly, and a decision about whether the correct check is per-iteration, or a bound on the accumulator, or something that subsumes both, and possibly a reconsideration of the option (a) I rejected on a cost argument that a falsified monotonicity claim partly undermines. Folding that into a dispatch about closing two other orders would be doing it badly because it was nearby, and RUL-0003 matter 5 is the reason I will not: 'recorded as closed when it was not' is the failure this studio keeps catching, and its cousin is 'ruled on in passing'. It comes to me as its own matter, with EVD-0006 as its evidence, and it is the first thing after the two gate-verdict records. I record my position now so my silence is not read as absence of one: my monotonicity argument was made falsifiable on purpose, it has been falsified, and I accept the finding without needing it re-demonstrated.

Until then, amended criterion 11 clause (2) is RATIFIED AS TO ITS PLACE IN THE ORDER AND NOT AS TO ITS TRUTH, and nobody may treat it as a settled requirement to implement against. That is a blocking condition below, and it is the reason this ruling's verdict is inconclusive rather than adequate.

rulings.matter: 5 -- the standing rule this leaves behind
rulings.ruling:
A RULING THAT REQUIRES A PROPERTY TO HOLD MUST ALSO SAY WHERE IT IS TO BE WRITTEN DOWN AND BY WHOM. RUL-0003 required seven things and said neither, and an author had to guess; it guessed in the direction that made the order gateable, which is the right direction, and it still had to guess. Effective immediately and binding on me first, since I wrote the ruling that failed it: every director's ruling that imposes a requirement on a dispatched order must state, for each requirement, whether it becomes an acceptance criterion of that order or remains a blocking condition of the ruling, and if the former, that the order's author is authorised to add it. Two extra clauses in a ruling, and they remove the only real justification an agent had for exceeding an authorisation.

The corresponding duty on the author side, stated so it is not inferred: adding an acceptance criterion to a dispatched order is a change to that order and must be reported as one, with a rationale in the order recording what was added and under what authority. Reporting that the other criteria are unchanged is not a report of what was done. The author already knows how to do this properly -- WO-0008's criterion 6 amendment, by the same agent, cites RUL-0001 matter 1 and PRO-0004 in the order's own rationale, quotes the original text verbatim so a reader can see what changed, and states that no other criterion is touched. That is the studio's good precedent, it was produced by this author, and WO-0010 needs the same treatment applied to seven insertions and a renumbering.

This is directed to whoever owns lesson promotion as a candidate, worded to be usable: 'An authorisation that scopes what may be changed must also scope what may be ADDED. An agent handed a ruling that requires things no criterion covers will either leave the order ungateable or widen it; both are failures of the ruling, not of the agent. State, per requirement, whether it becomes a criterion and who writes it.' It is a different lesson from L-003 and must not be merged with it.

criteriaAssessment.notes: I deliberately record no criterion grades for WO-0010 in this ruling, and the omission is the finding rather than an oversight. This adjudication is about the order's TEXT -- what was edited, by whom, under what authority -- and not about the delivery against it. Grading twenty-four criteria, seven of which have never been graded by anyone and one of which contains a justification EVD-0006 has falsified, would require a fresh technical adjudication of the WaveScheduler remedy that I have expressly declined to fold into this pass (matter 4). RUL-0002's and RUL-0003's assessments remain the live ones and I neither adopt, clear nor supersede them, with the essential caveat from matter 3: their grades are recorded by criterion NUMBER and the numbering has moved beneath them. Original criteria 12-17 are now 19-24; criteria 12-18 are new and ungraded; criterion 11 is amended and its violated grade stands. Anyone reading RUL-0002's or RUL-0003's criteriaAssessment against today's file without applying that mapping will attribute grades to the wrong criteria -- including reading criterion 16, graded satisfiedByInspection, as covering the non-over-rejection test, which is not written.

blockingConditions: AMENDED CRITERION 11 CLAUSE (2) STATES A JUSTIFICATION THAT EXECUTION HAS FALSIFIED. EVD-0006 records that the mandated single-first-step non-progress check, implemented exactly per RUL-0003, admits dt=33570436f at interval 2f / firstDelay 1f and then fails to terminate, confirmed in 17ms against the real WaveScheduler with a bounded buffer. The monotonicity argument now written into the order as an acceptance criterion is wrong. Nobody may implement against clause (2) as a settled requirement. This is ratified as to its PLACE in the order and not as to its TRUTH, and the corrected remedy is a fresh adjudication reserved to me with EVD-0006 as its evidence -- deliberately not resolved in this pass, for the reason in matter 4.

WO-0010's rationale must record the criteria change: seven criteria added at positions 12-18 transcribing RUL-0003 matter 2 clauses (i)-(iv) and matter 4, the parenthetical appended to the original criterion 12 (now 19) and why it was needed, and the resulting renumbering of the original 12-17 to 19-24. Cite RUL-0003 and this ruling as the authority. Follow the form this author already produced for WO-0008's criterion 6 amendment, which is the studio's good precedent. work-order-author's act, authorised here; the text of the criteria themselves is not to be touched again under this authorisation.

The mapping in matter 3 must be applied to RUL-0002's and RUL-0003's criteriaAssessment by whoever assembles WO-0010's gate packet. Those rulings are not to be edited -- a ruling is a judgement at a point in time and the record is corrected by adding to it, never by rewriting it.

All blocking conditions of RUL-0002 and RUL-0003 stand unaltered and are carried forward in full. I cleared, weakened and reordered none of them, and this ruling adjudicates the criteria edit only. Note that RUL-0003's first condition -- the CHA-0001 remedy -- is the one EVD-0006 has shown is not achieved by the shape RUL-0003 mandated, and it remains open on those terms until the fresh adjudication above.

G2 must pass on its own terms; nothing here touches it and no part of it is overridden. When it does, WO-0010 will additionally need the gate-verdict record that RUL-0005 matter 2 found the studio has never produced for any order.
nonBlockingLogged: The seven inserted criteria are substantively sound as transcriptions and I found no drift between them and RUL-0003's text on the points I checked -- the DtGuard-placement prohibition, the message-distinctness requirement, the ratchet's explicit refusal of CHA-0001's proposed 'completes and returns a finite count' form, and the non-over-rejection clause are all carried across with their reasoning intact rather than summarised away. Whatever the procedural fault, the transcription was careful.

The author reported truthfully against the wrong question. It was asked in effect 'did you change the other criteria' and answered accurately; nobody had told it that adding criteria or shifting numbering counted as a change. Matter 5 states the duty prospectively rather than charging it retrospectively.

The claim put to me that WO-0010's escalateIf covered this is not supported by the file: none of its five clauses concerns editing acceptance criteria. Recorded because it lowers the severity of the breach and because it is the kind of detail that hardens into fact if nobody checks it.

This is the second finding in one day where a claim reached me by transcription and was wrong in the transcribing -- the other being RUL-0004's arithmetic, corrected in RUL-0006 matter 1. Neither was concealment and both were caught by reading the primary source. Worth one line in the digest, not a work order.

boundariesObserved: I wrote no production code and no test code and touched nothing under Assets/**. I amended no acceptance criterion and I reversed none: I ruled on an amendment another agent had already made, and I directed the rationale that must accompany it rather than writing it, because recording an order's own change history is its author's act. I left Studio/orders/open/WO-0010.json byte-for-byte untouched. I did not re-grade WO-0010's criteria and said so explicitly rather than producing an assessment I had not earned; RUL-0002's and RUL-0003's stand and I neither cleared, weakened nor reordered any of their blocking conditions, including the one EVD-0006 has now shown is not met by the remedy my own ruling mandated. I did not edit RUL-0002 or RUL-0003 to repair the renumbering they suffer from, because rulings are corrected by adding to the record and never by rewriting it, and I would want that held against me as firmly as I hold it against anyone. I did not resolve the falsified monotonicity argument, which is a fresh technical adjudication and would have been done badly for being nearby. I marked nothing complete and signed no gate. I did not escalate to the founder: this is a first-round adjudication of one authorisation-scope question and settling it internally is the point of the role.
whyNoChallenge: The edit is defensible on its merits, the seven insertions faithfully transcribe requirements I myself imposed, and the parenthetical repairs a contradiction the same act created rather than introducing one. More decisively, the gap that let it happen is in RUL-0003 -- my own ruling required seven things and never said whether they were to become criteria or who was to write them -- so a challenge here would charge an agent for a hole I left, which would teach exactly the wrong lesson about what happens to an agent that resolves an under-specified instruction in the direction of making the gate work. qa-director had standing to challenge this and declined for a good reason it recorded in RUL-0004 matter 6, adding that it would file if the edit were allowed to stand WITHOUT a recorded rationale. That condition is met by this ruling and by the rationale it directs, which is the answer to its concern rather than a dismissal of it. The one genuinely serious finding in this pass -- a falsified justification standing in the order as though true -- is against my own reasoning in RUL-0003, and a director challenging itself is theatre where a blocking condition and a reserved adjudication are the honest instruments.
limitations: I have no shell, no git and no CI access; my instruments were file reading and search over the working tree. Four consequences. First, my reconstruction that WO-0010 went from seventeen criteria to twenty-four is inferred from the current file read against RUL-0002's and RUL-0003's cross-references by number -- notably RUL-0003 matter 5's 'all seventeen criteria', its grading of 15 and 17 as unevidenced, and its matter 2 reference to 'the manner PRO-0002 and criterion 12 require', which pins the original criterion 12 to what is now line 37. I could not run git diff to confirm it, and if the original count was not seventeen the mapping in matter 3 is wrong in its details though not in its existence. Second, I did not verify that the seven insertions are byte-faithful to RUL-0003's prose; I read them for substance and found no drift on the points I checked, which is a weaker claim than a diff would support. Third, I take EVD-0006's falsifying case on the record rather than re-deriving the arithmetic of dt=33570436f at interval 2f; that is deliberate, since RUL-0003 undertook to accept execution over derivation and re-litigating it would be the motion that undertaking exists to prevent. Fourth, my statement that WO-0010's escalateIf does not cover criteria edits rests on reading its five clauses as they stand today; if escalateIf was itself edited in the same act I would not be able to see it, which is one more reason the rationale record directed above needs to state everything that changed and not only the criteria.
